from_quote: it has been ſaid by Mr. Wilſon, and many others, that a ſtanding army is neceſſary for the dignity and ſafety of America
rationale: The paragraph names Mr. Wilson as saying that a standing army is necessary for the dignity and safety of America. WilsonSpeech.4 (Wilson's address of October 6, 1787, before this pamphlet) takes up the objection to a standing army in time of peace; the speech is not named, so the link rests on the speaker's name and the subject.
to_quote: no man, who regards the dignity and ſafety of his country, can deny the neceſſity of a military force

from_quote: ſtipulated by the preſident and two thirds of the ſenate
rationale: The paragraph speaks of treaties "stipulated by the president and two thirds of the senate," which describes the treaty-making clause; no other clause names the President, two thirds of the Senate and treaties together.
to_quote: by and with the Advice and Consent of the Senate, to make Treaties, provided two thirds of the Senators present concur

from_quote: guarantee a republican form of government to every ſtate in the union
rationale: The paragraph refers to the "promise to guarantee a republican form of government to every state in the union," which restates the wording of the guarantee clause without quotation marks.
to_quote: guarantee to every State in this Union a Republican Form of Government

from_quote: the new Congreſs are impowered to determine their own ſalaries
rationale: The paragraph names the power of Congress to fix its own salaries, which only the compensation clause of Article I, Section 6 addresses.
to_quote: to be ascertained by Law, and paid out of the Treasury of the United States

from_quote: the appellate juriſdiction of the ſupreme federal court
rationale: The paragraph names the appellate jurisdiction of the supreme federal court, which is the subject of the second clause of Article III, Section 2.
to_quote: the supreme Court shall have appellate Jurisdiction

from_quote: One repreſentative to thirty thouſand inhabitants
rationale: The paragraph states the ratio of one representative to thirty thousand inhabitants, the figure in the apportionment clause of Article I, Section 2.

from_quote: any regulations for the time, places, and manner of chooſing our own repreſentatives
rationale: The paragraph objects to Congress "interfering with any regulations for the time, places, and manner of choosing our own representatives," which echoes the wording of Article I, Section 4, Clause 1.
to_quote: The Times, Places and Manner of holding Elections for Senators and Representatives

from_quote: the circumſcribing the votes to only ten electors in this ſtate
rationale: The paragraph objects that votes for the first magistrate are limited to "only ten electors in this state," which refers to the appointment of presidential electors by each state.

from_quote: A ſenate choſen for ſix years
rationale: The paragraph speaks of "a senate chosen for six years," the term given in Article I, Section 3, Clause 1.

from_quote: the article which declares the ratification of nine ſtates ſufficient for the eſtabliſhment of the new ſyſtem
rationale: The paragraph identifies the article declaring "the ratification of nine states sufficient for the establishment of the new system"; it gives no article number, but only Article VII says this.
to_quote: The Ratification of the Conventions of nine States, shall be sufficient for the Establishment of this Constitution

from_quote: they wiſh for no federal city, whoſe "cloud cap'd towers" may ſcreen the ſtate culprit from the hand of juſtice; while its excluſive juriſdiction may protect the riot of armies encamped within its limits
rationale: The paragraph objects to a "federal city" with "exclusive jurisdiction," which describes the district over which Congress is given exclusive legislation in Article I, Section 8, Clause 17.
to_quote: exclusive Legislation in all Cases whatsoever
